setting: Velykyi Luh (the Great Meadow) on the lower Dnipro, late summer 1580: feather-grass steppe cut by dry balky (ravines) with willow-lined streams, oak groves, watch kurgans (mohyly) with small earth-and-timber outposts (horodky), wooden signal towers with tar barrels.

characters.ostap: 30-year-old Zaporozhian scout, lean and wiry, sunburnt narrow face, thin scar across the nose bridge, shaved head with dark brown forelock, long dark drooping mustache, linen shirt, short brown zhupan, dark blue sharovary, faded red sash, worn yellow boots, shablia
characters.saskos_horse: dark bay steppe horse with a white blaze, lathered with sweat, faded red saddle cloth
characters.bandits: renegade Cossacks in ragged mismatched clothes, patched grey svytas, greasy sheepskin vests, torn sharovary, rope belts, shaggy overgrown forelocks, unkempt stubble, old samopals, a bow, a lasso, a short rohach, shaggy horses
characters.bandit_leader: heavyset 45-year-old renegade, matted black beard and shaggy black hair, broken nose, looted faded crimson zhupan torn at the elbows over a dirty shirt, rope belt
characters.yas: 65-year-old retired Cossack veteran, bald head with a thin white forelock, long white mustache, deeply wrinkled leathery face, a notch missing from his left ear, patched faded blue zhupan, black sash
characters.kurinnyi: 50-year-old kurin commander, broad weathered face, grey forelock, thick grey mustache, crimson zhupan, black sash, black kalpak with fox fur, shablia at the hip
characters.cossack_riders: Zaporozhians with forelocks or fur kalpaks, long mustaches, blue and green zhupans, red and blue sharovary, samopals on their backs, sabres, sturdy steppe horses

palette: dusty ochre and straw-gold steppe, olive willows, dark oak green, pale hot sky; red sash and yellow boots as the only warm accents; grey musket smoke; evening scenes in amber firelight.
notes: Ostap rides his dead comrade Sasko's dark bay horse (white blaze) until the fight; afterwards he takes the outlaws' shaggy horses. The outlaws are renegade Cossacks, not Tatars: same cut of clothing but ragged, dirty and mismatched. Story text is extremely graphic; images keep violence implied (smoke, falling silhouettes, dust), never wounds. Punishments (hanging, burial) are suggested only by ropes on empty branches, graves and grim faces, never bodies.
